verdict.rationale: Trigger.dev's docs explicitly describe durable execution primitives that support resuming after failures: tasks are version-locked so mid-flight runs aren't disrupted by new deploys (docs-7), automatic retries with backoff (docs-4), waitpoint tokens that pause/resume runs (docs-6), and an explicit claim that tasks survive 'refreshes, deploys, and crashes' (docs-13), reinforced by the GitHub description of 'durable tasks, retries, queues and idempotency' (gh-1). Community testimonials corroborate reliability under real infra failure (e.g. Puppeteer OOM crashes handled gracefully, comm-9) though some earlier comments note wait/resume as a wishlist item, suggesting the capability matured over time rather than being present from the start. Missing for 10: independent hands-on verification of exact step-level state recovery for generic (non-chat) tasks after an infra crash, and more detailed documentation of checkpoint granularity.
